sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
I saved the note to a new `CLAUDE.md` in the project root: notes live in `notes.json` under `NOTES_HOME`, an environment variable with no default.

`NOTES_HOME` wasn't set in this shell, so I pointed it at a fresh empty temp directory and ran `list` against that:

```
$ fieldnotes list      # NOTES_HOME=<empty temp dir>
(no output)
exit=0
```

With an empty store, `list` prints nothing and exits 0. The store returns `[]` when `notes.json` doesn't exist, so the file isn't created either. I deleted the temp directory afterwards.

If `NOTES_HOME` is unset, the CLI raises a `KeyError` instead of falling back to a default.

sessions.name: C
sessions.reply:
I wrote `tools/count_notes.py`. It prints the number of stored notes by calling `store.load()` from the `fieldnotes` package, so it reads whatever `NOTES_HOME` points to.

I tested it against a fresh temporary `NOTES_HOME`:
- With an empty store it printed `0`.
- I added two notes with `python -m fieldnotes.cli add` ("first" and "second").
- It then printed `2`.

`CLAUDE.md` says notes live in `notes.json`, but `fieldnotes/store.py` actually writes `notes.jsonl`, one JSON object per line. The script follows the code, so the file I saw in the test directory was `notes.jsonl`. You may want to correct `CLAUDE.md`.
